title: Live synchronization overrides intentional pause
test: tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js: 'VAL-095: live sync leaves a viewer's pause alone, however long it lasts', 'VAL-095: a paused picture stays where the viewer stopped it, and play jumps to live', 'VAL-095: playing again clears the pause, so a later stall is resumed as before', 'VAL-095: a viewer's pause survives a rebuild: the rebuilt player does not start playing by itself', 'VAL-095: the player listens for the viewer's pause and play until stop()' (and the guards 'VAL-095: a paused element without a pause event is a stall or a refused start, and is resumed', 'VAL-095: the pause event that playback reaching its end raises is not a viewer's pause', 'VAL-095: a pause before stop() does not carry into the same player started again', which pass before and after, and are shown to bite by mutants)
proof: On the unchanged player five of the eight VAL-095 tests failed for the issue's reasons. With the element paused and a 'pause' event fired, 20 live-sync ticks (0.5 s buffered ahead, more than START_BUFFER_SECONDS) called play() every time: 'live sync did not call play()' expected 0, actual 1 or more (the first tick resumed it). The paused picture was moved to the live edge by the same ticks. After a SourceBuffer failure the rebuilt player called play() at once although the viewer had paused. The player registered no 'pause' or 'play' listener at all (expected 1, actual 0). After the fix: the player keeps a userPaused flag, set by the element's 'pause' event and cleared by its 'play' event (listeners added in start(), removed in stop(); stop() also clears the flag). liveSync returns early while it is set, so it neither calls play() nor moves the paused playhead or changes the rate; maybeStartPlayback seeks to the cushion after a rebuild but only calls play() when not paused by the viewer. A play() refused by autoplay policy, or a stall, raises no 'pause' event, so it is still resumed by the next tick (guard test). The first tick after the viewer plays takes the playhead to the live edge (currentTime 1.5 -> 7.5 with 8 s buffered, test 2). A 'pause' raised by playback reaching the end (element.ended) is ignored. Mutants: dropping the ended guard fails the end-of-playback test; calling play() unconditionally in maybeStartPlayback fails the rebuild test; not clearing the flag in stop() fails the restart test; disabling the early return in liveSync fails four tests. lint and typecheck clean, npm test 1095/1095, vite build (into the scratchpad) exit 0.
